title: Vuln triage automation KPIs and audit schema draft
content:
Purpose:
This working draft proposes a pragmatic automation surface for vulnerability scanner outputs -> triage -> evidence ingestion -> SIEM export, instrumented by KPIs and tied into the RBAC v2 audit schema. Goal is to reduce manual churn for low-confidence findings, ensure evidence is stored with immutable provenance, and make triage SLAs measurable and enforceable across Dedicated/Private deployments.

High-level objectives:
- Normalize scanner outputs from multiple tools (Snyk, Trivy, Dependabot, OSS-Finder) into a common envelope.
- Attach audit metadata (actor, tool, pipeline, timestamp, RBAC principal) to every ``evidence artifact`` we persist.
- Route low-confidence, noisy findings into an auto-dismiss queue with an SLA and automatic re-eval after code change.
- Export enriched events to SIEM with consistent fields so detection/alert rules are simple and stable.
- Track KPIs (time-to-first-triage, time-to-remediate, false-positive rate, evidence-attachment-rate).

Current pain points (observed):
- Each scanner emits different severity labels and identifiers; linking the same vuln across scans is brittle.
- Evidence (patches, PoC, package metadata) often stored in ad-hoc places; hard to prove remediation chain for audits.
- RBAC gaps: SRE runbooks and infra automation use different service principals; audit logs don't always capture which principal performed a suppression.
- SIEM mappings vary by ingestion team; dashboards drift when a field is renamed by a scanner integrator.

Proposed normalized envelope (textual example):
- We will normalize into a single line JSON-ish entry per finding before enrichment. Example (stored in Evidence DB):
  {
    "envelope_id": "env-20241105-0001",
    "scanner": "trivy",
    "scanner_finding_id": "TRV-@abc123",
    "canonical_vuln_id": "CVE-2024-XXXXX | REDWOOD-OV-217",
    "package": "libfoo",
    "version": "1.2.3",
    "severity": "high",
    "scanner_confidence": 0.76,
    "first_seen": "2024-11-05T09:14:00Z",
    "last_seen": "2024-11-05T09:14:00Z",
    "evidence_artifacts": ["s3://evidence/vuln/env-20241105-0001/patch.diff"],
    "source_commit": "d7f8a2c",
    "workspace": "prod-us-east-1",
    "detected_by_pipeline": "nightly-deps-scan",
    "triage_state": "auto-queued",
    "assigned_team": "eng-platform-deps",
    "audit_principal": "svc-deps-scanner@redwood-inference",
    "audit_timestamp": "2024-11-05T09:14:05Z"
  }

Normalization rules (summary):
- severity -> map to numeric score (critical=90, high=70, medium=40, low=10) for easier SLA bucketing.
- scanner_confidence -> 0..1 score from tool when available, else map heuristics (pattern match on title + repo metadata).
- canonical_vuln_id -> prefer CVE if present, else internal id with stable prefix (REDWOOD-OV-###).
- evidence_artifacts -> must include at least one immutable link (S3 preferrable, with content-addressed filenames).

Audit schema integration (RBAC v2 considerations):
- Every change to triage_state, suppression, or evidence attachment MUST create an AuditRecord with fields: event_id, actor_type (human|service), actor_principal, actor_roles (list), action, target_envelope_id, timestamp, request_id, source_pipeline, justification_note (optional).
- Example event for automatic suppression attempt:
  event_id: AUD-20241105-9001
  actor_type: service
  actor_principal: svc-auto-triage@redwood-inference
  actor_roles: ["vuln-triage-bot","deps-reader"]
  action: auto-suppress
  target_envelope_id: env-20241105-0001
  timestamp: 2024-11-05T09:15:02Z
  request_id: rq-9f3b
  justification_note: "confidence<0.2 && not-reachable-from-prod"

RBAC v2 edge cases to handle:
- Service principals used by Dedicated and Private customers: must be namespaced per-customer so that audit maps to tenant (e.g., svc-deps-scanner@tenant-acme).
- Human overrides require 2-step audit traces: request -> approval. Approval events must record approver principal and linked Jira ticket.
- Suppression TTL: auto-suppressed findings expire after 90 days unless changed; expiry event must be audited.

Evidence automation and retention policy (draft):
- Store immutable evidence artifacts for ALL confirmed HIGH/Critical findings. Retain 3 years minimum.
- For auto-queued/low-confidence items, store minimal metadata + truncated PoC (30 days retention).
- Evidence storage layout must be content-addressed and log the uploader principal + pipeline + fingerprint.
- Hashing algorithm: sha256 with hex prefix. Example artifact name: loot/sha256/3b4f.../env-20241105-0001/patch.diff

SIEM export schema (flattened fields expected by SOC):
- event_type: vuln.finding.created | vuln.finding.updated | vuln.finding.remediated | vuln.evidence.attached
- envelope_id
- canonical_vuln_id
- severity_score (numeric)
- scanner 
- scanner_confidence 
- workspace
- assigned_team
- triage_state
- audit_principal
- audit_event_id
- evidence_count
- remediation_ticket (JIRA)
- rule_source (e.g., snyk-fed, trivy-fed)
- customer_tenant (if applicable)

SIEM example log line (CSV-ish):
  2024-11-05T09:15:02Z, vuln.finding.updated, env-20241105-0001, CVE-2024-XXXXX, 70, trivy, 0.76, prod-us-east-1, eng-platform-deps, auto-queued, svc-auto-triage@redwood-inference, AUD-20241105-9001, 1, JIRA-VULN-4023, trivy-fed

Automation triage flows (suggested):
1) Ingestion -> normalize -> enrichment (link to code owner, package owner, dependency graph reachability) -> decide: auto-dismiss | auto-queue | open-ticket
2) Auto-queue: create a triage item in our internal tracker with SLA window = severity bucket (High = 72h, Medium = 14d, Low = 30d). If unchanged at 50% SLA, send reminders.
3) Auto-dismiss: if scanner_confidence < 0.15 AND historical false-positive rate for this scanner+pattern > 80%, mark as suppressed with audit event and set reeval trigger on next dependency update.
4) Open-ticket: create JIRA with prefilled fields, attach evidence artifact link, and mark remediation SLA (Critical=48h, High=7d, Medium=30d).

KPIs to instrument (initial):
- Time to first triage action (median, p95) — target median < 4h for critical/high.
- Time to remediation (median) — target critical < 48h.
- Evidence attachment rate (percent findings with >=1 artifact) — target 95% for high/critical.
- Auto-dismiss false-positive rate (measured monthly) — target < 5%.
- Average number of manual escalations per week.

Implementation notes / infra impact:
- Need a small "normalizer" lambda (or k8s pod) running a pipeline: pull -> normalize -> enrich -> write to evidence DB + emit SIEM event. Stateless transformer, can be horizontally scaled.
- Evidence DB: S3 + metadata in Postgres (envelope -> artifacts). Postgres row must be small (id, pointers, canonical ids) to avoid huge write amplification.
- Audit log service: append-only log (kafka topic + long-term S3 snapshots).
- RBAC v2 check: normalizer must call IAM to annotate principal role list. If missing, default to service principal only but emit a warning audit event.

Sample queries (Splunk/ELK) for SOC dashboards:
- Count of open high+critical findings by workspace in last 7 days:
  index=vuln_events severity_score>=70 triage_state!=remediated | stats count by workspace, severity_score
- Recent auto-suppressed events with low confidence (discover misconfig):
  index=vuln_events event_type=vuln.finding.updated action=auto-suppress | where scanner_confidence < 0.2 | table _time, envelope_id, scanner, scanner_confidence, audit_principal

Playbook snippets (for infra oncall):
- If a critical finding is in "open-ticket" for >24h with no code owner assignment, escalate to oncall-plat and create a runbook checkpoint.
- For suppressed findings that are later confirmed (manual re-open), annotate the suppression event with reviewer comment and link to retro ticket.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- SLA windows: agree if High triage SLA should be 72h or 48h (current product asks for 72h to avoid noisy escalations).
- Retention policy across Dedicated vs Private deployments: Private customers may require different retention, need opt-in config.
- Should we auto-create JIRA tickets in customer-managed trackers for Private installs? (data residency / permission implications).
- Which scanners are first-class supported for enrichment? Proposal: start with Trivy + Snyk + OSS-Finder, add others on demand.

Next steps (action items):
- Sync w/ Platform infra to prototype normalizer lambda (owners: Liam O'Connor, due 2024-11-20).
- Build minimal evidence DB schema and audit-topic contract (owner: Priya Nair, due 2024-12-05).
- Create initial SIEM event mapping and test with SOC ingest team (owner: Daniel Cho, due 2024-12-15).
- Draft RBAC v2 annotation schema and service principal naming convention for Dedicated/Private (owner: Ava Martinez, due 2024-11-18).

Notes-to-self / rough commands used in experiments:
- local normalizer run: python tools/normalize_scans.py --input sample-trivy.json --out normalized.json
- example mapping script: git rev-parse --short HEAD -> used to map evidence to commit sha

References:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Vuln-Playbooks
- Jira ticket for triage automation: JIRA-VULN-4023
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/892

Status: working draft, will be iterated after infra sync.

-- Ava
